Subject: Discovery recap - inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Aisha / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 30m discovery so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. Please reply if I misremember anything.

Top pain points (what you told us):
- Inference spend is the largest line item for your LLM product (real-time chat + on-demand summarization).
- High unit cost driven by limited batching, per-request cold starts, and multi-replica redundancy for availability.
- Lack of a prefix/KV cache because your serving layer is stateless; batching would require changes to your orchestrator.
- You haven't validated model quantization end-to-end yet — open to 8-bit/4-bit if quality holds.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Self-hosted on GCP (mixed N1 + A2/gpu instances) running a homegrown serving layer (Python + Triton) with Llama-2-13B for production.
- ~15M input+output tokens/month, peaks at ~1.8k rps during business hours.
- Estimated monthly inference spend today: ~$120k (including infra + ops).

Success criteria for a pilot / vendor evaluation:
- Reduce unit inference cost by ~2-3x vs current baseline while preserving customer-observed quality.
- 95th pctile latency under 300ms for chat flows (target).
- Clear measurement baseline and pass/fail criteria run on your canonical prompt set.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive (90m) with Dev and your infra engineer to review traffic shape, sequence lengths, and integration constraints. You suggested Wed Mar 24 at 10:00am PT — please confirm.
2) Redwood to run a 2-week pilot: we'll run a scoped proof-of-concept on a subset of traffic (approx 50k tokens/day) to demonstrate unit economics (batching + KV cache + quantization profile).
3) Deliverables: pilot pricing estimate, SOC2 summary, integration checklist, and a measurement plan (A/B vs baseline).
4) Procurement/Legal: Priyom (cc'd) will follow up with a draft SOW and standard commercial terms if pilot looks good.

Attachments: redwood_pilot_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (pilot pricing), SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level controls)

Thanks — I'll wait for confirmation on the Wed slot and any additional folks you want in the tech call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our token math: roughly 12-16M tokens/month (varies) — the $120k number includes infer + inference-related infra and a bit of overhead for cross-region replication. Our target is to get to <$40k/month (so ~3x reduction).
- Peak rps is closer to 2k (we saw short spikes to 3k during testing).
- We are open to aggressive quantization (4-bit) for non-prod and a careful rollout for prod if quality checks pass on our evaluation prompts.

Wed Mar 24 10:00am PT works for the tech deep-dive. Attendees from our side: me (product), Carlos (infra lead), and Lina Park (backend) — Lina will dial into the call. Could you share a short agenda and an integration checklist ahead of time? Also important to note: our legal/procurement team will want an initial SOW and an idea of pilot MRR commitments before starting the pilot (even if small). Carlos, looping you to confirm network/VPC access constraints.

On the attachments — we'll need the SOC2 summary and a sample SOW before procurement can formalize next steps.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Product | FinBot Inc
